cases.text:
name: gate-triage
description: Reads a failed run and proposes a fix.
owner: group:default/team-gate
kind: event
identity:
  type: workload
  serviceAccount: autopilot-runs/gate-triage
profile:
  tierCeiling: T1
  tools:
  - glidepath.runs.list
  - repo.file.get
  - repo.pr.open
  glidepath:
    apps:
    - gate-api
  repos:
    allow:
    - acme/gate-api
  models:
  - claude-sonnet-5-5
  network: clearance+model
  compute: small
  limits:
    ttlMinutes: 20
    toolCalls: 60
    githubCalls: 40
    openPrs: 1
    modelTokens: 400000
    children: 0
runtime:
  image: ghcr.io/acme/runtime@sha256:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
  framework: generic
  instructions: Find why the run failed.
triggers:
- type: event
  source: glidepath
  bindingKey: gate-api.pipelinerun.finished
  match:
    subject.content.outcome: failure
  maxPerHour: 4

cases.why: a pattern's `$` matches only at the very end of the text; Python's also matches before a final newline, so a value that ends in a newline passes a Python `^...$` pattern. A newline at the end of a name, a glob or an image is never intended, and a name that is not what the reviewer saw is what a match would be made on

cases.why: a pattern's `$` matches only at the very end of the text; Python's also matches before a final newline, so a value that ends in a newline passes a Python `^...$` pattern. A newline at the end of a name, a glob or an image is never intended, and a name that is not what the reviewer saw is what a match would be made on

cases.why: a pattern's `$` matches only at the very end of the text; Python's also matches before a final newline, so a value that ends in a newline passes a Python `^...$` pattern. A newline at the end of a name, a glob or an image is never intended, and a name that is not what the reviewer saw is what a match would be made on
